answer: The most convincing sybil defense binds each identity to a nonce-chained work history: every task is signed with a fresh nonce referencing the previous one, so reputation grows as a spiral rather than a tree. An attacker cannot hollow out one identity and fork it into parallel copies, since each branch shares past nonces that peers reject; juniper-fresh branches gain no trust until they re-earn history. Cost to an attacker: redoing the entire workload per identity, making fake agents pointless.
